thread:
elaine: quick sync note from RFC review: decision needed on auth enforcement for console query: inproc adaptor vs sidecar proxy. must weigh p99 impact, auditing, and rollout risk.

anya: inproc adaptor = best latency, preserves batching; but duplicates auth logic across services and languages. sidecar = single place for KMS/audit, easier compliance, but adds network hop and breaks same-proc batching.

matt: benchmark we ran: adaptor adds ~0.2ms median and ~0.8ms p99; sidecar adds ~1ms median and ~3.5ms p99. console interactive flows care about that p99.

raj: Dedicated tenants require tamper-evident audit trails and HSM attestation. sidecar simplifies that. adaptors can still log but increase integration work.

elaine: proposal: hybrid path. ship adaptors behind feature-flag for latency-sensitive paths; build shared auth-worker (unix-socket) so adaptor can call a local process, making migration to sidecar easier. maintain a sidecar Helm chart for Dedicated.

anya: +1. migration checklist: 1) adaptor interface + tests; 2) implement for console-query; 3) auth-worker shim; 4) helm chart for sidecar; 5) canary (5-10% traffic) with SLI checks; 6) runbook for fallback.

matt: sample helm values for infra: 
```yaml
consoleQuery:
  auth:
    mode: "adaptor" # adaptor | sidecar
    featureFlag: "auth-adaptor-v1"
    adaptorConfig:
      cacheTTLms: 200
      workerSocket: "/var/run/auth-worker.sock"
```

raj: I'll draft the compliance checklist for sidecar (audit fields, KMS flows).

ci-bot: Created ticket PLAT-9401 and PR #4801 (wip): auth-adaptor + auth-worker prototype - https://git.internal/repo/pulls/4801 :white_check_mark:

elaine: thanks all. will open RFC follow-up doc and schedule a short sync to review perf thresholds.
